comments.text:
🇧🇲 Would you live in Bermuda—an extremely rich paradise with NO rivers, NO freshwater lakes, and one of the highest living costs on Earth? 🤯
What shocked you most: the rainwater rooftops, pink-sand beaches, shipwrecks, or Bermuda’s incredible wealth? Share your country and opinion below! 👇

comments.author: @c.d.7742
comments.text: I live in Canada and have a cistern in the farmhouse basement built by my great great grandfather which I still use for hot water. There are no minerals in rainwater so there is never any buildup inside the water heater.  It's great for showering, washing laundry and dishes because it leaves no residue or water spots.  I use a well for cold water to drink and cook.

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: The sociological depth of this script is outstanding. It’s so rare for travel documentaries to look past the pink sand and expose the intense socio-economic paradox of the island. Explaining how Bermuda became immensely wealthy not by extracting resources, but by selling the world "protection against risk" through reinsurance [07:21], while simultaneously pricing locals out of their own homeland [09:07], adds such a profound, necessary layer to the story. Exceptional research and narrative structure! 👏
